title: Portfolio Settlement of Commercial Capacity Bidding Program Enrollments
content:
## Business customer program manual — Demand Response Programs

### 1. Portfolio rule

A business customer's Commercial Capacity Bidding Program enrollments on several service agreements form one portfolio. In each event, performance is judged on the portfolio's delivered kW against the sum of the portfolio's committed kW, and any shortfall penalty is shared among the enrollments in proportion to their committed kW, rounded to the cent with the remainder on the enrollment with the largest commitment. Capacity payments stay per enrollment. Other programs are judged per enrollment.

### 2. Terms used

- **Portfolio delivered kW** — for one event, the total of the delivered kW recorded for that event on all of the customer's Commercial Capacity Bidding Program enrollments.
- **Portfolio committed kW** — the total of the committed kW of those enrollments.
- **Share of an enrollment** — its committed kW divided by the portfolio committed kW.

### 3. Settling a portfolio penalty

(a) The portfolio's shortfall for the event is judged by comparing the portfolio delivered kW with the portfolio committed kW; the enrollments are not judged one by one.
(b) The penalty for the event is shared among the enrollments: each enrollment other than the one with the largest commitment bears the penalty multiplied by its share, rounded to the cent.
(c) The enrollment with the largest commitment bears the remainder — the event's penalty less the rounded amounts borne by the others — so that the shares add up exactly to the penalty.
(d) Each enrollment's capacity payment is still calculated on that enrollment's own committed kW.
(e) Enrollments in Peak Time Rebate, Smart Thermostat Rewards, the AC Cycling Program, Home Battery Dispatch and the Base Interruptible Program are judged per enrollment and never pooled.

### 4. Worked example (hypothetical portfolio)

A customer holds three Commercial Capacity Bidding Program enrollments: Site A committed 30 kW, Site B 20 kW, Site C 20 kW. Portfolio committed kW: 70 kW.

In one event the recorded delivered kW are 21 kW at Site A, 24 kW at Site B and 15 kW at Site C. Portfolio delivered kW: 60 kW, which is 10 kW short of the 70 kW portfolio commitment. Site B's delivery above its own 20 kW counts toward the portfolio total.

Suppose the event's penalty on that 10 kW shortfall is $85.00. It is shared as follows:

| Enrollment | Committed kW | Share | Unrounded amount | Amount borne |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Site B | 20 | 20 of 70 | $24.2857… | $24.29 |
| Site C | 20 | 20 of 70 | $24.2857… | $24.29 |
| Site A (largest commitment) | 30 | 30 of 70 | $36.4286… | $36.42 — the remainder, $85.00 less $24.29 less $24.29 |
| Total | 70 | | | $85.00 |

### 5. Points of judgement

- **A site delivering nothing, with the portfolio fully delivered.** Where the portfolio delivered kW meets the portfolio committed kW, the portfolio has no shortfall in that event, whatever one site delivered.
- **One enrollment only.** A customer with a single Commercial Capacity Bidding Program enrollment has a portfolio of one; its delivered and committed kW are that enrollment's own.
